text:
alex: quick follow-up to the MHA layout RFC — thinking about NHWC vs NCHW and whether QKV should be stored contiguous (Q,K,V interleaved) or separated. main concerns: kernel fusion opportunities, memory coalescing, and streaming KV cache implications. :thinking:

maria: can you clarify the exact layouts you mean? e.g. NHWC = [B, S, H, D] vs NCHW = [B, H, S, D]?

jin: yeah that's what i mean. in practice we care about head-major vs seq-major memory ordering. if we do [B, S, H, D] the seq dim is contiguous which helps GEMM->softmax->GEMM fused paths that expect S major. contiguous QKV (q,k,v interleaved per token) makes a single GEMM produce all three which is great for fusion. downside is KV cache streaming: to append new KV you either deinterleave on write or maintain a different cache layout.

leah: also important: stride and alignment. on GPU best throughput often needs 128B load alignment. that means head_dim should be padded to multiple of 8/16 depending on dtype. padding a lot kills memory for very long contexts.

sam: what's the ballpark overhead if we pad head_dim to 16? for 8k tokens and batch=1, tens of MBs?

jin: rough calc: extra_per_token = num_heads * (pad - raw_d) * bytes_per_elem. for 32 heads, pad 16->32 extra, with fp16 (2B) => 32*16*2 = 1kB per token. 8k tokens -> 8MB. multiplies across batches. so yes non-trivial.

alex: tradeoffs: contiguous QKV wins for training/fused GEMM paths and less kernel launches. separated Q/K/V (per head contiguous) wins for streaming KV cache and partial attention kernels (when we reuse K/V across many queries). also separated allows easier per-head quantization.

maria: about kernel impl — Triton/custom kernels can handle interleaved QKV by reading a single output tile and splitting, but that often uses more shared mem and registers. cublasLt fused attention expects certain layouts for optimal perf (it likes sequence-major contiguous).

leah: another practical point: many backends (TensorRT, onnxruntime) prefer NHWC-ish contiguous channel-last layouts for conv-like ops. for MHA the equivalent is seq-major ([B,S,H,D]). if we pick NCHW-ish ([B,H,S,D]) we make it awkward to drop into some vendor accelerators.

ops-bot: note: there is an internal benchmark ticket: INF-6423 benchmarking QKV layouts across Triton/cuBLAS/FP16. created by ops-bot.

sam: maybe we can have dual internal formats: compute_format = interleaved for fastest fused path, cache_format = per_head for streaming. conversion cost on cache write needs to be measured.

jin: agreed. conversion could be done on the write path (when first writing KV to cache) amortized, or via a tiny kernel that transposes blocks of size [heads, head_dim] — cheap compared to backend GEMMs. but watch out for small-sequence overhead.

alex: proposed API addition: add optional field in model config: "cache_format": "per_head" | "interleaved". default per_head for compatibility. runtime chooses to keep compute tensors interleaved. snippet:

```
model_config: {
  attention: {
    compute_layout: "interleaved",   # QKV fused
    cache_layout: "per_head",       # KV cache storage
    pad_head_dim_to: 8               # alignment hint
  }
}
```

maria: quantization note — interleaved QKV makes per-head quant nicer? actually the opposite: per-head scales are easier if heads are stored separately. interleaved forces mixed scales unless we quant by head and store scale metadata per head. more metadata but doable.

leah: cross-vendor nuance: ROCm kernels we've seen prefer different alignment rules; our runtime should expose an alignment knob per device. keep default conservative (pad to 8) and autotune per instance.

sam: microbenchmark plan? i can run short suite: 1) fused QKV GEMM latency for interleaved vs separated, 2) cache write+read streaming for long ctx, 3) memory overhead for padding, 4) quantized heads. results per-device (A100, H100, AMD MI).

jin: i'll help with kernel variants in Triton, build interleaved->per_head transpose kernel.

alex: awesome. next steps: sam to run benchmarks (assign INF-6423), jin to prototype transpose kernel, leah to collect alignment rules for target devices, maria to enumerate quant tradeoffs. we'll sync in 30m call. thanks all :+1:
